details:
Q1: What should happen when a file in the audit's scope is larger than the 2 MiB read-only snapshot limit?
Choices:
A) Give the oversized file to the audit agent in bounded, size-capped chunks so it can still read it. Fail the audit only if the file or the total goes over a hard upper cap. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Always fail the audit when any scoped file is left out (emit `security-audit` failure, no tracker/clean marker, no `passed` security-pass state).
C) Don't fail. Mark the result "incomplete coverage" instead of clean, list the omitted files on the tracker or in the findings JSON, and don't move the last-audited-commit marker forward or record a `passed` SHA.
Q2: Which files does the "never record a clean result while scoped files are omitted" rule cover?
Choices:
A) Only the files the audit was explicitly scoped to: the diff-range or incremental changed-file list, prior-finding files and fix-cycle diff files. Full-repository scans with no explicit scope just list the skipped oversized files as a coverage note. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Every tracked file, including full-repository scans (first runs, history rewrites, diffs over 200 files, `/re-security-pass` full-range audits).
**Note:** B together with Q1:B would make full scans fail on any repo that tracks a file over 2 MiB, such as large lockfiles or data fixtures, until that file is removed.
C) Like A, but skip known generated or lock files (for example `*-lock.json`, `*.lock`, `go.sum`) so they never trigger the rule.
